nodes.label: Storage Migration Technical Design (Kiro spec)
nodes.rationale: Low-level design for moving layouts from git-tracked JSON into Postgres LayoutCatalogue and masks/calendar assets into S3, organised by implementation phase (model+0016, S3Storage, view refactor, masks, asset_store, gitignore). Written before PR #111; the shipped code diverged in places (rename later retired, calendar-asset fallback replaced by CalendarAssetUnavailable, masks under a prefix).

nodes.label: LayoutCatalogue model design
nodes.rationale: name (unique, case-sensitive) is the identifier and overrides definition['name']; definition JSONField; product_type inferred at import; is_deprecated soft delete; version bumped per write; imported_at/imported_by co-validated in clean(). A separate LayoutPermission table was deferred because APIKey.can_list_layouts suffices.

nodes.label: Migration 0016_import_layout_catalogue
nodes.rationale: CreateModel plus RunPython import_layouts_from_filesystem reading backend/migrations/prod_layouts.json with update_or_create (idempotent); missing file -> WARNING and zero rows, non-array -> ERROR and skip, bad entry -> skip and continue. Reverse is an intentional NOP so rollback is STORAGE_BACKEND=local, not a DB rollback.

nodes.label: export_layout_catalogue.py export script
nodes.rationale: Run on prod before deploy to bake the live catalogue into prod_layouts.json; reads from the DB if LayoutCatalogue exists, else from the filesystem, forcing definition['name'] to the filename stem.

nodes.label: S3Storage backend design
nodes.rationale: Fails fast with ImproperlyConfigured on missing AWS env; list_layouts() queries Postgres never S3 LIST; assemble_chunks uses multipart upload_part_copy and aborts the MPU on any part failure so an in-progress upload is not billed forever; layouts_dir()/masks_dir() are markers only.

nodes.label: services/asset_store.read_asset typed reader
nodes.rationale: Single entry point for calendar_styles / calendar_palettes / holidays / fonts reads so the backend (local vs S3) is transparent to CalendarStylesView, HolidaysView and _read_fonts; rejects unknown asset types with ValueError.

nodes.label: Layout cache keys: layouts_list_all, ops_layouts_list_all, layout_detail:{name}:{surfaces}
nodes.rationale: All keys and 120 s TTLs preserved across the migration so no frontend change was needed; pe: is the Redis KEY_PREFIX. GetLayoutView and EditorInitView share the detail key so either warms the other.
nodes.norm_label: layout cache keys: layouts_list_all, ops_layouts_list_all, layout_detail:{name}:{surfaces}

nodes.label: Property 2: Rename atomicity
nodes.rationale: select_for_update() on the old row inside transaction.atomic() so no request observes both old and new names as non-deprecated. Superseded: renaming was retired 2026-09-16 and name is now immutable.

nodes.label: Property 3: Migration idempotency
nodes.rationale: Applying 0016 twice on a populated table leaves the same rows because the import uses update_or_create(name=...).

nodes.label: Property 4: STORAGE_BACKEND=local full bypass (rollback path)
nodes.rationale: Designed so setting STORAGE_BACKEND=local restored disk-based layout serving without a DB rollback. The shipped code did not keep this: views query LayoutCatalogue with no disk fallback and storage/layouts/ was deleted (CLAUDE.md 'Backwards Compatibility').

nodes.label: Property 5: Mask copy-before-delete
nodes.rationale: On rename an S3 mask key is never deleted before a successful server-side copy; copy failure -> 500 with the original untouched, delete failure after copy -> orphan logged and 200.

nodes.label: Mask serving via presigned S3 redirect
nodes.rationale: MaskDownloadView checks the path guard, head_objects the key, and 302s to generate_presigned_url (1 h); S3 errors are a 502 without detail. Prod has since moved to a CloudFront CDN redirect with presigned URLs as the fallback when S3_CDN_DOMAIN is empty.
nodes.norm_label: mask serving via presigned s3 redirect

nodes.label: read_calendar_asset S3-then-local fallback
nodes.rationale: Designed to serve the local seed on any S3 failure with a WARNING. Later found unsafe: an outage or a deleted key would resurrect the seed, so S3Storage.read_calendar_asset now raises CalendarAssetUnavailable on errors and honours tombstones; only NoSuchKey/AccessDenied count as absent.

nodes.label: Cache invalidation errors never propagate to the write
nodes.rationale: invalidate_layout_caches wraps delete_many and delete_pattern; AttributeError (non-Redis backend) falls back to the unparameterised key, other errors log WARNING. Lists are cleared even if the detail glob fails.
nodes.norm_label: cache invalidation errors never propagate to the write

nodes.label: Storage Migration Requirements (Kiro spec)
nodes.rationale: Thirteen EARS-style requirements for moving layouts to Postgres and masks/calendar assets to S3 behind a StorageBackend switch, preserving every API contract so no frontend change is needed. Motivated by perpetual git conflicts from the ops UI rewriting tracked files at runtime.

nodes.label: Req 1: LayoutCatalogue data model
nodes.rationale: Byte-for-byte case-sensitive uniqueness on name ('hero' and 'Hero' distinct), indexes on name/product_type/is_deprecated/is_public, imported_at and imported_by set together or not at all.

nodes.label: Req 2: Migration 0016 schema creation and data import
nodes.rationale: Idempotent upsert from prod_layouts.json; missing file is a WARNING and success with zero rows; reverse is a NOP.
nodes.norm_label: req 2: migration 0016 schema creation and data import

nodes.label: Req 3: S3Storage backend implementation
nodes.rationale: Fail at startup (ImproperlyConfigured) on missing AWS env rather than at first S3 call; list_layouts never lists S3; multipart assembly aborts on failure.

nodes.label: Req 4: ListLayoutsView refactoring
nodes.rationale: Query is_deprecated=False, is_public=True; merge definition with name and hasCalendar; 120 s layouts_list_all cache whose write failure never errors the request; ?fields=summary via _summarize_layout.

nodes.label: Req 5: GetLayoutView refactoring
nodes.rationale: Path traversal guard first (400 before any DB query), 404 on DoesNotExist, layout_detail:{name}:{surfaces} cache, case-insensitive surfaces filter returning an empty array rather than 404.

nodes.label: Req 6: LayoutManagementView refactoring
nodes.rationale: Upsert with update_or_create (201 create / 200 update), soft delete via is_deprecated, cache invalidation after every write, atomic rename with 409 on conflict (rename later retired in code).

nodes.label: Req 7: Atomic cache invalidation
nodes.rationale: Bulk-delete both list keys, glob-delete layout_detail:{name}:*, fall back on AttributeError, log WARNING and never propagate on any other failure.

nodes.label: Req 8: Mask serving via presigned URLs
nodes.rationale: Redirect to a presigned URL (300-3600 s) under S3, FileResponse under local, guard first, 404 on missing, 502 without S3 detail on service errors. Specifies 301 where the design and code use 302.
nodes.norm_label: req 8: mask serving via presigned urls

nodes.label: Req 9: Mask upload to S3
nodes.rationale: Guard the filename, upload under masks/, embed the S3 key in the layout definition, copy-before-delete on rename.

nodes.label: Req 10: Calendar assets migration to S3
nodes.rationale: read_calendar_asset(asset_type, asset_name) on StorageBackend; S3 key ops-config/{type}/{name}; local path {STORAGE_ROOT}/{type}/{name}; S3 miss falls back to local with a WARNING (later tightened in code).

nodes.label: Req 11: Deployment and rollback
nodes.rationale: Migration applies automatically via migrate --noinput at container start; rollback is STORAGE_BACKEND=local with the table left intact for re-promotion.

nodes.label: Req 12: API contract preservation
nodes.rationale: GET /api/layouts, GET /api/layouts/{name}, masks and POST /api/ops/layouts/{name} return identical shapes and status codes so no frontend code changes; masks stay on the embed allowlist without a privilege gate.

nodes.label: Req 13: JSON round-trip fidelity
nodes.rationale: definition stored in a JSONField must compare == after a round trip, preserving Unicode, nesting and floats; POST accepts a dict or a JSON string parsed with json.loads (400 on failure).

nodes.label: Path_Traversal_Guard (_is_safe_layout_name)
nodes.rationale: Rejects names containing /, \, .. or a leading .; kept after the migration as an injection guard for DB names and S3 keys and run before any DB or S3 call. Now the shared is_safe_layout_name in api/views/_common.py.

nodes.label: Soft_Delete via is_deprecated
nodes.rationale: DELETE sets is_deprecated=True instead of removing the row, preserving the audit trail while hiding it from public reads.

nodes.label: CSP enforcement plan
nodes.rationale: Status report-only. First claimed 'production-ready' on 2026-09-10; that run missed Google Fonts being blocked (fixed PR #168, 2026-09-29) and the described switch flipped only one of the policy's two halves. Corrected 2026-10-08.

nodes.label: CSP report-only mode
nodes.rationale: Violations are POSTed to /api/csp-report but nothing is blocked, except frame-ancestors on /editor/layout/* which is already enforced to limit who may embed the editor.

nodes.label: Two CSP halves, one CSP_REPORT_ONLY flag
nodes.rationale: Django (django-csp, CSP_* in settings.py) reads the flag at runtime for API/JSON and the Scalar page; Next.js (headers() in next.config.mjs) reads it at image build time via a compose build arg. A directive change must be made in both files; the policy needs 'unsafe-eval' for Fabric.js and Google's domains for sign-in and fonts.
nodes.norm_label: two csp halves, one csp_report_only flag

nodes.label: Sentry is the CSP violation history
nodes.rationale: CSPReportView logs a warning and sends a Sentry message; the backend log is lost on every container recreate (every ./deploy.sh). GET /api/celery/monitor/ carries no CSP reports, so an earlier 'no violations' check against it could not have found any.
nodes.norm_label: sentry is the csp violation history

nodes.label: Pre-enforcement checklist
nodes.rationale: Exercise every affected page with the console open (editor via embed token, iframe on an allowed origin, dashboard, /editor/layouts and the calendar/book ops editors, /login with Google, /docs/api/), then let several quiet days of real Sentry traffic pass; a short manual pass is not proof.

nodes.label: Flip-to-enforcement procedure
nodes.rationale: Set CSP_REPORT_ONLY=False in prod .env (backed up), run ./deploy.sh (rebuilds the frontend image; up -d or a backend restart flips only Django), verify both halves emit Content-Security-Policy via curl -sI on /login and /api/config, watch Sentry; roll back by flipping to True and deploying again.

nodes.label: History: the 2026-09-10 CSP test run
nodes.rationale: Local report-only run: Django headers on /api/config and /api/embed/session/validate, Next.js headers on the editor route, Fabric canvas rendering, iframe under frame-ancestors, pe:render_job arriving, dashboard and ops pages loading with no console violations. It did not exercise Google Fonts.

nodes.label: Product Editor README
nodes.rationale: Top-level overview: standalone print-file generator with dashboard download or HMAC-signed webhook delivery, no OMS push. Follows .env.example as the configuration source of truth.

nodes.label: Technology stack
nodes.rationale: Django 5 + DRF, Postgres 16 (tuned shared_buffers/work_mem), Pillow at 300 DPI, Celery 5 + Redis 7 split broker db 0 / cache db 1 so allkeys-lru can't drop task messages, Gunicorn gthread; Next.js 16 standalone, React 19, TS 5.7 strict, Fabric.js 7.2 lazy-loaded, Tailwind 3.4, Service Worker; nginx 1.27 edge with Cloudflare Origin Certificate.

nodes.label: Docker Compose services
nodes.rationale: backend, frontend, celery-worker-standard (the only worker; consumes priority,standard), celery-beat (GC every 6 h at 00/06/12/18 UTC), redis, db, proxy.

nodes.label: Quick start (local dev)
nodes.rationale: Fresh clones crash-loop the proxy until a TLS cert exists in proxy/nginx/certs; generate a self-signed one or let deploy.sh bootstrap it. .env.local overrides compose env; INTERNAL_API_URL must be http://backend:8000/api inside Docker.

nodes.label: Two server-side proxies (embed and internal)
nodes.rationale: /api/embed/proxy/[...path] for the customer iframe (X-Embed-Token) and /api/internal/proxy/[...path] for dashboard + editor (NextAuth cookie + INTERNAL_API_KEY); neither exposes an API key to the browser.

nodes.label: Direct partner generation (POST /api/layout/generate)
nodes.rationale: Always async, order_id mandatory, 202 with status_url; soft_proof / tiff_cmyk / callback_url body params removed in v1.8; direct callers poll render-status and never get a webhook.

nodes.label: Webhook delivery (embed flow only)
nodes.rationale: Opt-in via callback_url at POST /api/embed/session; notify_caller_webhook_task POSTs the payload with X-Signature: sha256=<hmac> keyed by the caller's api_key. README shows the pre-split payload without the three per-part download URLs that INTEGRATION.md documents.

nodes.label: Async queue architecture
nodes.rationale: At-least-once (acks_late + reject_on_worker_lost), 3 retries with 2/4/8 s backoff tracked in RenderJob.retry_count, MemoryError/soft limit fail fast, order resubmit upserts, on_commit dispatch failure marks the job failed, webhook as separate task retried 5x then requires_manual_review, single render path for embed and dashboard.

nodes.label: Migrations table (0001-0020)
nodes.rationale: Lists 0001 through 0020_layoutcatalogue_display_name; CLAUDE.md is ahead at 0021_layouttemplate.

nodes.label: Production checklist and required env
nodes.rationale: DEBUG=0, strong DJANGO_SECRET_KEY, AUTH_SECRET (compose aborts without it), EMBED_INTERNAL_SECRET, INTERNAL_API_KEY with its own value (never NEXT_PUBLIC_), Cloudflare Origin Certificate with Full (strict), firewall 80/443/22.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting table
nodes.rationale: Jobs stuck queued -> check worker and Redis; ClientFetchError on login -> INTERNAL_API_URL; dashboard 500 -> missing INTERNAL_API_KEY in .env.local; webhook failing -> CanvasData.requires_manual_review after 5 failures.

nodes.label: storage/ directory layout
nodes.rationale: uploads/, layouts/, masks/, exports/ with retention from stored expires_at and EXPORT_RETENTION_DAYS; chunks staged under UPLOADS_DIR/.chunks/<upload_id>/. Stale: layouts live in Postgres since PR #111 and masks in S3 on prod.

nodes.label: Environment variables reference
nodes.rationale: Grouped tables: core runtime, database, API keys and auth, frontend/proxy (incl. CSP_REPORT_ONLY), storage/uploads/retention, Redis/workers/Gunicorn, audit retention. INTERNAL_API_KEY equal to DIRECT_API_KEY skips the INTERNAL seed with a warning.

nodes.label: Knowledge graph usage (graphify-out/)
nodes.rationale: Query the graph before grepping; refresh with scripts/graphify-refresh.py (AST only, keeps doc nodes and community names); never graphify update . or --update, which re-add stale doc nodes and unname communities.

nodes.label: Security summary
nodes.rationale: Bearer keys with per-key flags, embed tokens exchanged server-side, internal proxy gated by NextAuth + INTERNAL_API_KEY, proxy-side guard required for destructive ops routes (Django IsOpsTeam alone is insufficient), UUID v4 guards, audit trail in api_requests, Retry-After on 429.

nodes.label: Calendar Feature PRD
nodes.author: Kanna
nodes.rationale: Historical design record for the v1.12 foundation (server-side overlays) and v1.13 calendar product; where it disagrees with code, code wins. Two things shipped differently: cells are one flat ISO-date map, and photo canvases are capped at 12 with month i using photo (i mod N).

nodes.label: Calendar primitive (layout-agnostic positioned region)
nodes.rationale: A {x,y,width,height}-percent region inside any canvas owning only grid, cells, pills, holidays and per-cell editing; frames and artwork stay with the layout, so desk, full-page, poster and side-by-side calendars come free via layout authoring. Layout-authored, customer-overridden.

nodes.label: Minimal customer-facing controls principle
nodes.rationale: Every knob is a chance for an off-brand print; 'templates, not configurators' costs less to maintain, produces fewer support tickets and protects print quality. Font, grid, week-start and position stay ops-locked; customer gets theme, Gen-Z palette, calendar type and cell contents.

nodes.label: Overlays preview-only gap (server drew no text/shape/image)
nodes.rationale: engine.py had zero ImageDraw/ImageFont imports, so TextOverlay/ShapeOverlay/ImageOverlay appeared in thumbnails and vanished from the printed PNG/PDF. Pre-existing and unrelated to calendars, but a hard prerequisite for shipping one.
nodes.norm_label: overlays preview-only gap (server drew no text/shape/image)

nodes.label: Phase 1 Server-side overlay rendering (v1.12)
nodes.rationale: Built as services/overlay_renderer.py (render_overlays) plus services/fonts.py, wired into _composite_canvas after frame compositing and before the paper mask. Ships on its own and unblocks every existing overlay type, not just the calendar.

nodes.label: ISO-date keyed cell entries (flat product-wide map)
nodes.rationale: Shipped as one flat { iso_date: [CellOverride] } map instead of the 12-slot cellsPerCanvas array, so photo-canvas count changes and English/Financial flips can never lose or misplace entries; legacy 12-slot arrays are still read on restore.
nodes.norm_label: iso-date keyed cell entries (flat product-wide map)

nodes.label: Photo to month mapping (month i uses photo i mod N, cap 12)
nodes.rationale: Frontend caps photo canvases at 12 and the engine renders exactly 12 outputs; one photo cycles to every month, 12 map one-per-month, so upload order matters. An earlier build produced 12·N files in the ZIP.
nodes.norm_label: photo to month mapping (month i uses photo i mod n, cap 12)

nodes.label: Calendar grid rendering algorithm (identical client/server math)
nodes.rationale: firstCellOffset, totalCells (28/35/42), cellW/cellH, weekday header, per-cell override drawing, grid lines — computed the same way in lib/calendar.ts and calendar_renderer.py so preview matches print.
nodes.norm_label: calendar grid rendering algorithm (identical client/server math)

nodes.label: Calendar z-order slot (above overlays, below mask)
nodes.norm_label: calendar z-order slot (above overlays, below mask)

nodes.label: Auto-fit text via ImageFont.getbbox binary search
nodes.rationale: No library fits either side: DOM auto-fit libraries measure via getBoundingClientRect and cannot see a Fabric canvas; Pillow has no fitting helper. ~15 LOC binary search over getbbox is the documented community pattern.
nodes.norm_label: auto-fit text via imagefont.getbbox binary search

nodes.label: Cell images reuse smart-crop + MediaPipe auto-orientation
nodes.rationale: Each cell is a tiny frameSpec, so calculateSmartCropOffsets (client) and the _composite_canvas cover-fit math (server) apply unchanged, and the v1.11 pose pipeline already corrects sideways uploads — zero new cropping or orientation logic.
nodes.norm_label: cell images reuse smart-crop + mediapipe auto-orientation

nodes.label: Pill-style cell entries with rotating 3-slot dotCycle
nodes.rationale: Date number always visible; entries stack as pills with one theme-wide background and a dot colour rotating by entry index, so multi-entry cells stay distinguishable without exposing a colour picker (per the minimal-controls principle).
nodes.norm_label: pill-style cell entries with rotating 3-slot dotcycle

nodes.label: Global holiday auto-load (holidaySource)
nodes.rationale: storage/holidays/<locale>/<year>.json seeded for en-IN and generic × 2026–2030; layout opts in via calendar.holidaySource {enabled, locale}. showInCells shipped as a checkbox nothing read and was removed 2026-09-29.

nodes.label: Nager.Date holiday source
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the seed source at PRD time; later found to have no India coverage (HTTP 204) and replaced by the offline holidays package behind manage.py refresh_holidays.

nodes.label: Three style presets (modern-minimalist, modern-genz, weekday-highlight)
nodes.rationale: Stored as JSON under storage/calendar_styles/; ops picks one when authoring, its style block is copied into the layout. weekday-highlight says one thing — Sundays are different (#FEE2E2 fill, #DC2626 number).

nodes.label: Gen-Z palettes (Butter & Purple, Mint & Hot Pink, Lilac & Coral, Sky & Lemon)
nodes.rationale: Each palette sets all six colour roles together plus a 3-slot dotCycle; the swatch is the only Gen-Z customisation control. New palettes ship as JSON files under storage/calendar_palettes/genz/ with no code change.
nodes.norm_label: gen-z palettes (butter & purple, mint & hot pink, lilac & coral, sky & lemon)

nodes.label: Calendar as Multi-Surface Product (productType: calendar)
nodes.rationale: A separate product category would fork render, ops and preview pipelines; pure multi-surface would force ops to hand-build 12 surfaces and keep theme/type in sync. A productType tag on existing multi-surface plumbing (per-surface dispatch, N-file ZIP, single webhook) is the whole architectural cost.

nodes.label: Single-template authoring + 12-surface auto-gen
nodes.rationale: Ops designs one representative month; the layout stores that template and materialize_surfaces expands it into 12 surfaces at render time, only (year, month) varying unless a surfaceOverride says otherwise.

nodes.label: Surface index to (year, month) resolution formula
nodes.rationale: totalOffset = surfaceIndex + (monthOffset ?? 0); realMonth = ((startMonth-1+totalOffset) % 12)+1; realYear = baseYear + floor((startMonth-1+totalOffset)/12). Handles both 12×1 and 1×12 modes uniformly.
nodes.norm_label: surface index to (year, month) resolution formula

nodes.label: Per-surface overrides (surfaceOverrides, field-level replace)
nodes.rationale: Sparse map keyed month_ii; effective(surface) = template ⊕ override. Fields replace rather than deep-merge because merging arrays (by id? concatenate? positional?) is ambiguous and every interpretation leaks to UX. frames, calendar position and overlays may be overridden; canvas, themePreset, calendarType, weekStart may not.

nodes.label: Auto-rolling year (defaultYear: current)
nodes.rationale: Resolved at editor mount so layouts never freeze to a year and need no ops intervention each January; Financial type uses the previous calendar year as base when today is Jan–Mar. Shipped as resolveDefaultYear / resolve_default_year with a parity fixture.

nodes.label: English vs Financial calendar type (startMonth 1 vs 4)
nodes.norm_label: english vs financial calendar type (startmonth 1 vs 4)

nodes.label: productType as extension point (photobook etc.)
nodes.rationale: Multi-surface is the generic substrate for 'designed once, replicated N times with per-instance data'; each productType gets its own ops and preview UIs while storage and render layers are shared. Photobook was named as the next candidate and became the Book PRD.

nodes.label: calendars[] plural primitives (multi-surface vs poster mode)
nodes.rationale: count=12 × 1 calendar (desk/wall) or count=1 × 12 calendars with monthOffset (year-on-one-poster); validator enforces monthRange.count × calendars.length === 12.
nodes.norm_label: calendars[] plural primitives (multi-surface vs poster mode)

nodes.label: Cell-image expiry re-upload prompt
nodes.rationale: Cell images follow the UploadedFile GC; a GC'd image renders blank with an inline 'Image expired — please re-upload' prompt rather than any automatic recovery.

nodes.label: Calendar type flip warning modal
nodes.rationale: Entries outside the new 12-month range are hidden, not deleted — they stay keyed by ISO date and re-render if the customer flips back.

nodes.label: Fail-all-or-nothing multi-surface render failure
nodes.rationale: If 1 of N surfaces fails the whole RenderJob fails, partial outputs are cleaned up and the error names the month; retry re-renders all N. Per-surface retry deferred to v2.

nodes.label: Single bundled font Inter Variable, no picker (§11.7, reversed 2026-10-13)
nodes.rationale: Original rule: one bundled Inter-Variable.ttf for all text so preview and print cannot drift and 'font missing' cannot happen. Reversed 2026-10-13 for text overlays, which now print in the chosen Google font via services/google_fonts.py; Inter remains the default and the calendar grid font.
nodes.norm_label: single bundled font inter variable, no picker (§11.7, reversed 2026-10-13)

nodes.label: Feb 29 entries on non-leap years (hidden, toast)
nodes.norm_label: feb 29 entries on non-leap years (hidden, toast)

nodes.label: Hard cap of 3 entries per cell, no overflow badge
nodes.norm_label: hard cap of 3 entries per cell, no overflow badge

nodes.label: User-first MAX_ENTRIES precedence
nodes.rationale: User entries fill the 3 slots first, holidays take what remains, overflow is silently suppressed. Reverses the original holidays-first rule: customer intent beats auto-injection.

nodes.label: Validator rejects banned surfaceOverrides fields
nodes.rationale: banned = {themePreset, calendarType, weekStart, canvas, monthRange}; 400 names the field so manual JSON edits cannot bypass the layout-global rule.

nodes.label: IST-only renderer timezone with ISO date strings
nodes.rationale: The renderer never calls datetime.now(); 'today' is computed client-side in Asia/Kolkata only for year derivation. All v1 customers are in India.
nodes.norm_label: ist-only renderer timezone with iso date strings

nodes.label: No layout versioning — fresh load per embed
nodes.rationale: Each session loads the current layout; acceptable because calendar sessions are short and ops rarely edits published layouts. Add layoutVersion and lock active orders if edit frequency rises.

nodes.label: Calendar S3-Readiness Audit
nodes.rationale: Phase 9 audit (PRD §11.17), 2026-05-24, amended four times: the 'no hardcoded paths' conclusion held but reads bypassed S3 until 2026-09-29; production has run STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 since 2026-09-04; the transition-path section is historical.

nodes.label: STORAGE_ROOT-derived storage paths
nodes.rationale: One env var; LAYOUTS_DIR (legacy — layouts now in Postgres), EXPORTS_DIR and UPLOADS_DIR derive from it.

nodes.label: Calendar asset paths (palettes, styles, holidays, fonts.json)
nodes.rationale: Font .ttf files ship with the image under services/fonts_assets/, not STORAGE_ROOT — immutable assets, deliberately.
nodes.norm_label: calendar asset paths (palettes, styles, holidays, fonts.json)

nodes.label: S3 calendar asset key mismatch (missing prefix/.json)
nodes.rationale: read_calendar_asset built a key with neither S3_PREFIX nor the .json suffix write_calendar_asset adds, and render-time readers opened STORAGE_ROOT directly, so under S3 every read fell back to local disk and an ops edit reached neither preview nor print. Fixed by routing all readers through asset_store and sharing one key via _calendar_asset_key. Live on prod but no edit had been lost (zero writes in the audit trail).
nodes.norm_label: s3 calendar asset key mismatch (missing prefix/.json)

nodes.label: Tombstone deletes for calendar assets
nodes.rationale: A removed S3 key read as 'never written' and resurrected the git seed; a delete now leaves a tombstone object so only a key S3 has never held reaches the seed.

nodes.label: Fail-closed S3 reads (CalendarAssetUnavailable)
nodes.rationale: Any S3 failure other than NoSuchKey/AccessDenied raises instead of serving the seed: 503 in the preview, a retried render in the print — never a quietly wrong calendar.

nodes.label: Git-seeded local files as S3 default
nodes.norm_label: git-seeded local files as s3 default

nodes.label: refresh_holidays command + offline holidays package
nodes.rationale: scripts/refresh-holidays.py wrote local disk only (under S3 it merged into and rewrote the stale seed) and used Nager.Date, which has no India data; replaced by manage.py refresh_holidays reading and writing through storage from the offline holidays package.

nodes.label: Local-filesystem atomic writes (tempfile + os.replace)
nodes.source_location: Engine output paths, ZIP delivery, S3 transition path
nodes.rationale: The single concrete-storage assumption: engine PNG/PDF output and ZIP building stage a tempfile in the destination dir then os.replace. S3 PutObject is already atomic, so these would become temp → upload → delete.

nodes.label: Proposed blob_store.py shim (never built)
nodes.rationale: services/storage.py (S3Storage/LocalStorage) plus services/asset_store.py took that role; layout JSON moved into Postgres so write_layout_json_atomic no longer exists.

nodes.label: Autosave blanked CanvasData.image_paths every 2 s via update_or_create defaults
nodes.rationale: The browser never sees server paths so the autosave body carries none; CanvasStateView.put wrote image_paths or [] into defaults, so the purge found no files, deleted rows and reported files_deleted: 0 while 6.4 GB of photos stayed on disk across 265 orders. render_state['image_paths'] survived only because migration 0008 separated submit from autosave.
nodes.norm_label: autosave blanked canvasdata.image_paths every 2 s via update_or_create defaults

nodes.label: Option A: write image_paths only when the caller supplies it
nodes.rationale: Stops the bleeding with no migration, but does nothing for rows already blanked or for abandoned uploads; pinned by services/tests/test_erasure_contract.py.
nodes.norm_label: option a: write image_paths only when the caller supplies it

nodes.label: Option B: UploadedFile.order_id linkage recorded at upload (migration 0011)
nodes.rationale: Makes erasure provable — delete every UploadedFile where order_id = X needs no cooperation from canvas state — and reaches abandoned uploads that were never placed in a canvas. Populated from X-Order-ID or the request; direct-API uploads record blank. Backfill (phase 3) waived because the instance was fresh-start reset with 0 rows when 0011 landed.
nodes.norm_label: option b: uploadedfile.order_id linkage recorded at upload (migration 0011)

nodes.label: Option C: filesystem discovery sweep in the purge (viable only after per-order paths)
nodes.rationale: Uploads were stored flat with a random prefix so no path->order mapping existed; without one a sweep either misses files or deletes another order's. Once uploads moved to UPLOADS_DIR/<order_id>/ the purge deletes the directory outright — verified against a file with no UploadedFile row at all. _no_order/ is excluded and keep_paths (shared originals) still wins.
nodes.norm_label: option c: filesystem discovery sweep in the purge (viable only after per-order paths)

nodes.label: order_id '..' matched the identifier regex — path segment needs its own check
nodes.rationale: order_id permits '.', so '..' passed validation and the purge's rmtree would have targeted the parent of the uploads root. upload_subdir() rejects dot-only/dot-leading names and order_upload_dir() re-checks the resolved path stays inside UPLOADS_DIR; six traversal cases pinned in test_erasure_contract.py. A regex written for identifiers is not automatically safe as a filesystem name.
nodes.norm_label: order_id '..' matched the identifier regex — path segment needs its own check

nodes.label: _no_order/ bucket for direct partner API uploads
nodes.rationale: Direct-API uploads happen before any order exists, so they belong to no order; excluded from directory deletes and cleaned by the GC on age.
nodes.norm_label: _no_order/ bucket for direct partner api uploads

nodes.label: Large File Split Plan
nodes.rationale: Two files (api/views.py at 4,500 lines, editor page.tsx at 5,558 lines) conflicted across concurrent sessions, could not be read in one pass, and hid long-range interactions such as the PR #166 autosave-overwrite bug. Done 2026-10-06..07.

nodes.label: Part 1: api/views.py -> api/views/ package
nodes.rationale: Three PRs (#189, #190, #191) split one 4,500-line module into system, ops, media, layouts, layout_admin, calendar_assets, render, downloads, embed, uploads; __init__.py only re-exports so urls.py, tests and management commands keep importing from api.views.

nodes.label: Part 2: editor page.tsx split into hooks and components
nodes.rationale: 13 split PRs (A, B1-B4, C1-C8) after a safety net, riskiest last (persistence C8 highest). page.tsx went 5,558 -> 622 lines; it keeps shared state, hook calls in original order, and markup.
nodes.norm_label: part 2: editor page.tsx split into hooks and components

nodes.label: views/_common.py shared constants module
nodes.rationale: Module-level constants shared across submodules (LAYOUT_ID_NOTE, OPS_WRITE_AUTH, UUID_GUARD) and the shared is_safe_layout_name guard live here; it imports nothing from the package because a submodule importing from api.views would be circular.

nodes.label: Move, don't change (split PR rule)
nodes.rationale: A split PR only relocates code with the same dependency arrays and no new eslint-disables; bugs or duplicates found along the way get their own PR so a regression points at one change.

nodes.label: Patch the submodule, not the api.views re-export
nodes.rationale: patch('api.views._write_holidays') stops intercepting once the view lives in api.views.calendar_assets because the re-export is a second reference; tests such as test_ops_write_routes.py and test_csp_report.py must target the submodule.
nodes.norm_label: patch the submodule, not the api.views re-export

nodes.label: Editor page Jest characterization suite (Phase 0a)
nodes.rationale: Renders the whole page under Jest/happy-dom against a FakeBackend that records requests in order and can hold a response back; every key test was proven able to fail by breaking the guarded rule in page.tsx (8 deliberate breaks). Must pass unchanged across every split PR.

nodes.label: Playwright editor smoke suite (Phase 0b)
nodes.rationale: Covers what Jest cannot run: a fake storefront page receiving pe:back / pe:render_job, the enforced frame-ancestors policy, a real server render to a ZIP, imposition, real image decoding including HEIC, a phone profile. Local only because GitHub Actions is billing-locked.

nodes.label: Detached download links fix
nodes.rationale: Three download helpers (handleQuickDownload, the dashboard ZIP hand-off in executeServerRender, downloadBlob in lib/zip-utils.ts) attached a temporary <a> to document.body; all now click a detached <a>, which every current browser can download from (PR #195).

nodes.label: Keep effect order when extracting hooks
nodes.rationale: Effects run in declaration order and some depend on it (latest-value ref mirrors), so a hook is called where its first effect used to be; the Escape handler sits after useImposition because it reads that state.
nodes.norm_label: keep effect order when extracting hooks

nodes.label: One owner per ref
nodes.rationale: A ref belongs to the hook that writes it; anything else receives it explicitly. duplicateFills and intentionalDupesRef stay in page.tsx because the memo reads the ref during render, which the React Compiler lint rejects outside that file.

nodes.label: Before/after proof for backend split PRs
nodes.rationale: OpenAPI schema byte-identical between main and branch, every api.views name still importable, URL patterns resolve to the same classes, all tests pass, and two live servers (pe-split:before / pe-split:after images on the compose network) answer the moved endpoints identically on one database.
nodes.norm_label: before/after proof for backend split prs

nodes.label: Deploy each split PR soon after merge
nodes.rationale: Decided 2026-10-07 so a regression points at one PR; C4-C8 deployed outside Indian business hours; rollback is git revert + ./deploy.sh.
nodes.norm_label: deploy each split pr soon after merge

nodes.label: Sticky toolbar pinning fix (B3 prerequisite)
nodes.rationale: The toolbar never pinned when scrolled: the IntersectionObserver was set up once, before the toolbar existed (it renders only after the layout loads), through a plain ref nothing re-ran. The sentinel is now held in state through a callback ref (PR #207).

nodes.label: Append-only baseline log
nodes.rationale: Each entry is a dated snapshot against a commit; never edit an old row to 'correct' it, add a run. Numbers are only comparable on the same machine.

nodes.label: RateLimitMiddleware 200 req/60s per IP
nodes.rationale: RATE_LIMIT = 200 is set that high because a 200-photo calendar legitimately fires ~600 API calls in under a minute. A flood of /api/layouts returning 429 is the limiter working, not a throughput number.

nodes.label: 2026-07-11 c2babbe baseline (health 3859 rps @50, layouts 753 rps @10)
nodes.rationale: ApacheBench keep-alive on the dev Docker stack; /api/health is unthrottled so it is the raw proxy+gunicorn ceiling.

nodes.label: Manual design preflight checkpoint (1-3 h per order, fixed-capacity team)
nodes.rationale: Exists because the legacy system had no customer preview and no automatic quality/quantity validation; stalls orders on customer response, misses the 3 PM courier cutoff, causes cancellations and cannot scale with volume.

nodes.norm_label: target: under 5 minutes upload-to-production, zero human intervention

nodes.label: Track A: customer-facing preview and quantity validation before checkout
nodes.rationale: The customer self-validates by approving the preview; empty frames, auto-fill/pick-to-fill and the over-quantity modal replace the preflight count check.
nodes.norm_label: track a: customer-facing preview and quantity validation before checkout

nodes.label: Low-resolution (effective DPI < 150) warning, non-blocking
nodes.rationale: Replaces preflight's 'is this file good enough' judgement; informs but never refuses the order; the estimate mirrors the placement maths of both renderers (src/lib/dpi-utils.ts).

nodes.label: Standalone generator: no internal OMS push (push_to_production_estimator_task retired v1.9)
nodes.rationale: The embed webhook gives the storefront everything it needs to attach files to the order, and the storefront already talks to OMS via its own integration; OMS_PRODUCTION_ESTIMATOR_URL was removed and dashboard renders enqueue zero downstream tasks.
nodes.norm_label: standalone generator: no internal oms push (push_to_production_estimator_task retired v1.9)

nodes.label: CMYK / soft-proof / ICC pipeline removed in v1.8; colour handled invisibly via image_loader
nodes.rationale: Output is PNG (default) or PDF only; the promised CMYK colour-space warning never shipped. Instead services/image_loader.py colour-manages every upload ICC->sRGB so Display-P3 and AdobeRGB photos stop shifting in print without the customer knowing what a profile is.
nodes.norm_label: cmyk / soft-proof / icc pipeline removed in v1.8; colour handled invisibly via image_loader

nodes.label: B2: Celery + Redis async render queue (standard worker, retries, GC task)
nodes.rationale: Synchronous generation held a Gunicorn thread for the whole render and blocked concurrent orders at festival peaks; the API now answers 202 with a job id and status URL and the render happens in a worker pool.
nodes.norm_label: b2: celery + redis async render queue (standard worker, retries, gc task)

nodes.label: B1: two-layer canvas state persistence (editor_state JSON + IndexedDB File blobs keyed by orderId/fileId)
nodes.rationale: Files do not serialise, so each gets a UUID fileId and the raw blob goes to IndexedDB; auto-restore rehydrates originalFile so a refresh recovers the full editing context. Quota is per-origin, so very large jobs are best submitted in one session.
nodes.norm_label: b1: two-layer canvas state persistence (editor_state json + indexeddb file blobs keyed by orderid/fileid)

nodes.label: B4: server-side chunked upload + render for every Submit/Download (threshold removed v1.8)
nodes.rationale: Client-side Fabric rendering of >20 canvases caused timeouts, blank frames and crashes on low-RAM devices; a single unified server contract handles webhooks, large batches and resumable uploads identically.
nodes.norm_label: b4: server-side chunked upload + render for every submit/download (threshold removed v1.8)

nodes.label: B3: SKU-to-layout mapping built then removed 2026-09-04 (printo.in owns resolution)
nodes.rationale: printo.in resolves SKU -> layout itself and passes the layout name into the embed session, so a second mapping here was one more thing to keep in sync; it was never populated. Both smoke tests assert /api/sku-layouts/ returns 404.
nodes.norm_label: b3: sku-to-layout mapping built then removed 2026-09-04 (printo.in owns resolution)

nodes.label: API key bundle leak closed: NEXT_PUBLIC_DIRECT_API_KEY replaced by server-side internal proxy
nodes.rationale: The key was extractable from any browser's DevTools; all dashboard/editor calls now route through /api/internal/proxy gated by the NextAuth cookie, with INTERNAL_API_KEY server-only.

nodes.rationale: Under-upload must never block because a wrong caller-supplied qty would strand a real order. The server half is deliberately narrower than the browser's and fails open.
nodes.norm_label: order quantity (qty) rule: hard cap over, warn under

nodes.label: Calendars measure against their own photo count, not qty
nodes.rationale: A session's qty counts calendars bought, not photos.
nodes.norm_label: calendars measure against their own photo count, not qty

nodes.label: API key daily request cap (IST day, Redis counter, 429)
nodes.rationale: Blank means no cap and 0 blocks. entrypoint.sh does not seed a value so an admin-set cap survives deploys.

nodes.label: postMessage contract (pe:render_job, pe:back, pe:restore_*) with locked targetOrigin
nodes.rationale: pe:back exists because an iframe shares the tab's session history: history.back() inside the frame can walk the parent off printo.in mid-checkout.
nodes.norm_label: postmessage contract (pe:render_job, pe:back, pe:restore_*) with locked targetorigin

nodes.label: Restore manifest (restore.json on RenderJob.restore_manifest)
nodes.rationale: Per job because a second submit replaces render_state while the first job's files stay what they were. On the row, not a file in the export folder, because a loose file would outlive the retention clock until the orphan sweep found it.

nodes.label: Upload by link (POST /api/upload/from-url)
nodes.rationale: The customer's device never downloads and re-uploads a restored photo. The link comes from the browser, so the host must be on the API key's list, the connection pinned to a public address with no redirects, and size counted while reading. A repeat fetch for the same photo and order returns the copy held.

nodes.label: Held photo preview (GET /api/photos/<upload_id>/preview)
nodes.rationale: Default 1600 px because a card is drawn at up to 0.75x the layout canvas on a high-resolution phone. An embed session is served only its own order's photos.

nodes.label: Restoring a design from the embedding page (restore_order_id)
nodes.rationale: Our server never sees the reference; the page decides whether this customer may have that order. It runs inside the one restore so autosave stays off until the page has answered, and this order's own saved design wins.
nodes.norm_label: restoring a design from the embedding page (restore_order_id)

nodes.label: Restored previews never print (stand-in files)
nodes.rationale: A stored preview would come back after a refresh as an ordinary photo and be uploaded in the original's place, so stand-ins are never written to IndexedDB and are submitted by the server upload's id.

nodes.rationale: Everything through the proxy presents the shared ops-flagged INTERNAL_API_KEY, so a Django permission class sees one privileged identity whoever is signed in.

nodes.label: Django admin SSO via nginx auth_request + signed identity headers
nodes.rationale: Without the signature anything reaching backend:8000 on the Docker network could mint itself superuser.

nodes.label: Three frame renderers - the drift trap
nodes.rationale: Anything drawn inside a frame exists in three implementations; adding a feature to one silently disagrees with the other two.
nodes.norm_label: three frame renderers - the drift trap

nodes.label: Overlay fonts are Google Fonts only; ops retire rather than delete
nodes.rationale: The print allows active and retired fonts so a design never loses its font; a listed font that fails retries then fails rather than printing in another font.
nodes.norm_label: overlay fonts are google fonts only; ops retire rather than delete

nodes.label: No font fallback in print or editor (print file, then blank font)
nodes.rationale: A browser borrows a missing glyph from the device, so emoji and Tamil previewed fine and printed blank (printo job 6795066). Not Google's copy of the family: it is cut by unicode-range and lacks characters the print file has, so the editor would hide text that prints.
nodes.norm_label: no font fallback in print or editor (print file, then blank font)

nodes.label: Canvas editor removes unprintable characters and says why
nodes.rationale: Decision 2026-11-05. The toast exists because the note alone was missed on production. An unanswered check is retried after 1, 3 and 8 seconds because one request met a 502 during a deploy and the emoji stayed. Saved cards are never rewritten; they get a badge and a pre-submit notice.

nodes.label: GC expiry wave diagnosis (why every 6 hours)
nodes.rationale: The nightly 02:00 UTC sweep ran just before the 03:00-12:00 expiry wave and collected 2% of pending rows; effective retention was about 4 days while the sweep was healthy. Two wrong root causes came first; plotting expiries by hour found it.
nodes.norm_label: gc expiry wave diagnosis (why every 6 hours)

nodes.label: Why GC status records stale AND failing
nodes.rationale: Recording only successes made 'the sweep broke' and 'was never dispatched' look identical, which let a wrong diagnosis run two days on 2026-08-14.
nodes.norm_label: why gc status records stale and failing

nodes.label: Orphaned export directories incident
nodes.rationale: Cleanup filtered on status=completed, so a job killed mid-render lost its only file pointer when the cascade removed the RenderJob; 62 directories stranded by 2026-08-13.

nodes.label: Layouts moved from diverged disk to Postgres
nodes.rationale: Production had diverged from git (20 deleted, 11 renamed layouts); every pull touching a layout failed and git reset would have resurrected obsolete products. The audit after PR #111 found four paths still reading disk.
nodes.norm_label: layouts moved from diverged disk to postgres

nodes.label: Ops rename broke printo.in embed (2026-09-16)
nodes.rationale: name was both ops-editable text and the identifier printo.in hardcodes; a rename 404'd the embed. Fixed by an alias (renamed_to), then retiring renames in favour of display_name.

nodes.label: Where a restored design's previews come from (four designs in a day)
nodes.rationale: CDN previews hit CORS, egress objections followed, printo then sent originals only. Server fetch became acceptable through source_key reuse (one fetch per order); Kannan chose 1600 px after reading the card draw size.
nodes.norm_label: where a restored design's previews come from (four designs in a day)

nodes.label: Upload by link design reasoning
nodes.rationale: Phone re-upload meant about 1 GB each way for 200 photos. The host list is on the API key, not per session, because a key holder could send any value; the pin is released after headers because the webhook lock would serialise downloads in threaded web workers.

nodes.label: restore.json reasoning (column on RenderJob, not a loose file)
nodes.rationale: The old archive listed windows not photos, named entries by colliding file names and held frame photos only. A loose file would outlive retention because the GC deletes only files it has rows for.
nodes.norm_label: restore.json reasoning (column on renderjob, not a loose file)

nodes.label: Qty header-trust gap (PR #144)
nodes.rationale: The cap read X-Order-Qty, so a direct POST with the real key skipped it (qty=5, 7 files, 202).

nodes.label: Embed allowlist was prefix-only until 2026-09-03
nodes.rationale: fonts, holidays and calendar-styles accept ops writes upstream and the proxy injects the real key, so an embed token behind an ops-flagged key could PUT holiday data.

nodes.label: API key daily cap existed unenforced until migration 0022
nodes.rationale: Enforcing stored numbers would have capped production on deploy (hundreds of autosave PUTs per customer), so existing values were blanked and the default became no cap.
nodes.norm_label: api key daily cap existed unenforced until migration 0022

nodes.label: Dual-mounted write views gap (PR #163)
nodes.rationale: CalendarStylesView and HolidaysView write handlers never check the route, and the proxy gated only ops/* and fonts, so Editor-tier sessions could write through the aliases.

nodes.label: Login callbackUrl open redirect (PR #302)
nodes.rationale: The login actions returned callbackUrl unchecked to window.location, a hop NextAuth's redirect callback never sees.
nodes.community_name: Small group: Login callbackUrl open redirect (PR #302)

nodes.label: Overlay drift fix (PR #258)
nodes.rationale: fontSize was scaled by canvas height / 800 in the print only, and the three renderers had three wrapping models; shapes also differed in size and placement.

nodes.label: Emoji in a caption did not print (job 6795066)
nodes.rationale: A browser borrows missing glyphs from the device, the print uses one font file. A check redrawing overlays with render_overlays agreed by construction and missed it. Led to the blank font, the print's own font file in the editor, and removal with a toast.

nodes.label: Indian scripts in the print via Raqm (2026-11-06)
nodes.rationale: libfribidi0 turns Raqm on, but Pillow then defaults every font to it and English moved 47 px at 100 px; basic layout is now named explicitly and Raqm requested only for overlays holding an Indian script.
nodes.norm_label: indian scripts in the print via raqm (2026-11-06)

nodes.label: Print sheet and two mask slots decision (2026-10-26)
nodes.rationale: One mask with Mask on Export could not make a physical frame product: the frame baked in or white around the window. Bleed can never be a default because the retro polaroid's white border is the product; a typed rectangle was dropped since unseen artwork could only differ from what was ordered.
nodes.norm_label: print sheet and two mask slots decision (2026-10-26)

nodes.label: Icon tiles as broken images: Iconify rate limit (2026-11-05)
nodes.rationale: Each tile was a browser request to Iconify; about 180 icons then 429 for five minutes, and submit drew from the same host. Late answers for partial words also replaced the right result, so older answers are dropped.
nodes.norm_label: icon tiles as broken images: iconify rate limit (2026-11-05)

nodes.label: S3 paths that were never live (prod storage findings)
nodes.rationale: Calendar reads never hit S3 until 2026-09-29, masks printed from local disk only until 2026-10-12, the CDN had no DNS record and the IAM user lacked PutObject. A removed key resurrected the seed; hence tombstones.
nodes.norm_label: s3 paths that were never live (prod storage findings)

nodes.label: One template for several layouts (2026-10-28)
nodes.rationale: Tag matching was dropped because a sticker can land on a face under a different window arrangement; the key is the bleed-inclusive window box, matching is explicit ticks, artwork is placed by mm offset from the box centre.

nodes.label: A template faces one way (2026-10-29)
nodes.rationale: A turned layout hid every template with no message while the badge still counted them. Kannan's rule: never turn a design to fit, show none rather than a turned one.

nodes.label: Importing designs from the older design tool
nodes.rationale: Each old design is a layout plus a template. Separate stickers would take every click meant for the photo, so pictures merge into one Artwork sheet with per-pixel hit testing; artwork stays vector; the fetch uses the key's allowed_photo_hosts, not a setting.
nodes.norm_label: importing designs from the older design tool

nodes.label: Calendars lacked month names and never asked for 12 photos (2026-10-17)
nodes.rationale: No UI ever set calendar.monthTitle, so pages printed unlabelled; banners ran off qty, which calendars are exempt from, so 4 photos silently repeated across 12 months.
nodes.norm_label: calendars lacked month names and never asked for 12 photos (2026-10-17)

nodes.label: Upside-down previews from photos stored sideways (2026-10-25)
nodes.rationale: The lite pose model read 5 of 14 complaint photos. The short-range face detector's keypoints are coherent only on an upright face, so the turn with an upright face answers; its score does not. 11 of 14 read, none wrong.
nodes.norm_label: upside-down previews from photos stored sideways (2026-10-25)

nodes.label: Embed session could read another order's design (fixed 2026-11-05)
nodes.rationale: All of a company's customers share its key and the address carries ?order_id=, so the key alone never proved ownership. Reported by printo, reproduced with two sessions under one key.
nodes.norm_label: embed session could read another order's design (fixed 2026-11-05)

nodes.label: P1 autosave payload bloat (PR #134)
nodes.rationale: Base64 previews averaged 16 MB; 1,569 400s over 27 days, invisible because renders use render_state. Fixed by stripping previews, not raising the limit, which would trade silent failures for gunicorn OOM.

nodes.label: Autosave overwrote saved designs on a slow restore (PR #166)
nodes.rationale: A restore GET slower than the 2 s debounce let autosave PUT pre-restore state; the guard was off in the embed and calendar/book writers had none. Chrome masks it by holding same-URL PUTs.
nodes.norm_label: autosave overwrote saved designs on a slow restore (pr #166)

nodes.rationale: The only doc with an external audience; the product editor is a standalone generator that pushes nothing into an OMS, so the storefront's handler completes delivery. notify_caller_webhook_task wins if it disagrees with this doc.

nodes.label: X-Signature HMAC-SHA256 of raw body
nodes.rationale: Signed with the api_key over the raw bytes; a parsed-then-restringified body never verifies, and skipping the check lets anyone who knows the URL forge order completions. Compare in constant time.

nodes.label: qty_summary webhook field
nodes.rationale: Counts are server-derived from the submission; only customer_acknowledged_shortfall reflects the editor UI. It is the only guaranteed count a storefront can rely on.

nodes.label: Calendar qty_summary measured against pages
nodes.rationale: For a calendar, qty is how many calendars were bought and says nothing about photos, so ordered_qty is the photos the layout needs for every page to have its own.

nodes.label: Split download URLs (print / mock / uploads)
nodes.rationale: Added for storefronts that keep mock and print in separate fields; served by a ?content= filter over the same rendered files, so nothing is duplicated on disk. download_url is not deprecated.

nodes.label: Webhook retry policy (6 attempts, 2^n backoff)
nodes.rationale: 10 s webhook timeout with retries means handlers must enqueue the download and return 200 fast; a synchronous download creates duplicate downstream work.

nodes.label: ZIP fetch with Bearer auth
nodes.rationale: 404 on mock_download_url is deliberate rather than a valid-looking empty ZIP, so a storefront never stores a 22-byte archive against an order.

nodes.label: Print file size follows the bleed area
nodes.norm_label: print file size follows the bleed area

nodes.label: restore.json in the uploads archive
nodes.rationale: Product Editor keeps nothing past retention, so a company wanting a later reopen or reorder keeps its own copy of the uploads archive. editor_state is opaque to the partner, and the editor keeps reading every schema_version it ever wrote.

nodes.label: callback_url session field
nodes.rationale: No domain allowlist: auth is enforced by the api_key and HMAC. Must be https and at most 2000 chars.

nodes.label: order_id required on every embed session
nodes.rationale: Ties the session to one order, so the editor reads and saves that order's design and no other.
nodes.norm_label: order_id required on every embed session

nodes.label: qty session field
nodes.rationale: Moved off the iframe URL because the URL is browser-editable and nothing server-side honours it; 0 is an error rather than unlimited because it would cap every order at nothing.

nodes.label: Qty rule: over blocked, under warns
nodes.rationale: qty comes from the caller; a hard gate in both directions would let one wrong value strand a real order at checkout.
nodes.norm_label: qty rule: over blocked, under warns

nodes.label: A template faces one way (facing, templateCounts)
nodes.rationale: Nothing is turned to fit; a template_id the session's orientation would hide is a 400 at the call, so a customer never lands in the editor without the promised template.

nodes.label: Layout identifier is permanent and stable
nodes.rationale: A rename used to break embeds outright with no notice; name is now immutable, and displayName carries the cosmetic product name.
nodes.community_name: Small group: Layout identifier is permanent and stable
nodes.norm_label: layout identifier is permanent and stable

nodes.label: orientation session field
nodes.rationale: Turns a layout a quarter turn clockwise so nobody creates a second layout. Never makes a session or order fail; must not be sent until Printo has confirmed the layout prints correctly turned.

nodes.label: orientation report on webhook and editor/init
nodes.rationale: The session call cannot report applied because the layout is named only in the iframe URL.
nodes.norm_label: orientation report on webhook and editor/init

nodes.label: Layout tag keys (tagKeys, ?tag=)
nodes.rationale: Store and match on the immutable key because ops may rename a tag; tags are never deleted, so a stored key keeps resolving.

nodes.label: Photo host opt-in per API key
nodes.rationale: Off until the company names an exact host. The server fetches each photo once per order, so the customer's device never loads from the company's storage and no CORS setting is needed. Redirects are not followed.
nodes.norm_label: photo host opt-in per api key

nodes.label: restore_order_id on the iframe address
nodes.rationale: The reference is the company's own and our server never receives it; the embedding page decides whether this signed-in customer may have that order. Every reorder is a new session, order id and job.

nodes.label: pe:restore_request message
nodes.rationale: Asked once as the editor opens with a 10 second wait; silence reads as none / timeout and the customer gets an empty editor, so the page must always answer.

nodes.label: Daily request cap (429 until midnight IST)
nodes.norm_label: daily request cap (429 until midnight ist)

nodes.label: pe:render_job postMessage
nodes.rationale: Purely for the storefront's waiting UX and best-effort; file delivery happens by webhook, so it must not be relied on for fulfilment.

nodes.label: pe:back postMessage
nodes.rationale: An iframe shares the tab's one session history, so browser-back inside the frame could walk the customer off the parent site mid-checkout; the parent decides what Back means. A safe no-op until a listener exists.

nodes.label: Book / Booklet / Photobook Layout Creator PRD
nodes.norm_label: book / booklet / photobook layout creator prd

nodes.label: productType book, materialized like a calendar
nodes.rationale: Reuse the calendar's materialize architecture, not its renderer: expanding one template into N pages is the same problem as into 12 months, while month-grid drawing is not reusable.
nodes.norm_label: producttype book, materialized like a calendar

nodes.label: Separate book creator UI
nodes.rationale: Customer-variable page count, ordered pairs and thinking in spreads are a different mental model and a different screen, the reasoning that gave the calendar its own route.

nodes.label: D1: flat page list, not leaves
nodes.rationale: The renderer, ZIP contract and canvases_meta already speak one surface, one file. Deriving spreads for preview is cheap; deriving pages from sheets for the renderer is a permanent tax.
nodes.community_name: Small group: D1: flat page list, not leaves
nodes.norm_label: d1: flat page list, not leaves

nodes.label: D2: customer-entered page count in a template range
nodes.rationale: First product where surface count is customer state. Bounded by pageCount {min,max,step,default}; books step in multiples of 4 because of how signatures fold.
nodes.norm_label: d2: customer-entered page count in a template range

nodes.label: Hold page overrides when the count shrinks
nodes.rationale: Restored if the count goes back up, mirroring how the calendar keeps Feb 29 entries through a non-leap year.
nodes.norm_label: hold page overrides when the count shrinks

nodes.label: D2a: author one cover and one inner page
nodes.rationale: The author lays out an inner page and the materializer stamps it N times; pageOverrides stays the escape hatch.
nodes.norm_label: d2a: author one cover and one inner page

nodes.label: D3: flow in order, blanks stay blank, warn on overflow
nodes.rationale: Short-fill leaves blank pages because people leave pages for writing; warn-and-proceed, never block, consistent with submit-guards.
nodes.norm_label: d3: flow in order, blanks stay blank, warn on overflow

nodes.label: D4: covers authored separately, addressed by role
nodes.rationale: Addressed by role rather than index so a page-count change cannot renumber them; outside the customer's page count.
nodes.norm_label: d4: covers authored separately, addressed by role

nodes.label: Computed spine width
nodes.rationale: Settled 2026-10-17 as pageCount/2 x paperThicknessMm + 2 x coverThicknessMm, per-sheet thickness; the early pageCount x paperThicknessMm sketch double-counts. Recomputed on every count change; a wrong formula prints an unusable cover (R2).

nodes.label: D7: canvas per role
nodes.rationale: A hardcover wrap is larger than its block; the engine already reads canvas per surface, so differing sizes cost nothing there.

nodes.label: One ZIP with covers named to sort first
nodes.rationale: Chosen over a separate archive part so the partner webhook payload needs no change.
nodes.norm_label: one zip with covers named to sort first

nodes.label: D5: one gutterMm mirrored by page parity
nodes.rationale: One inner template is stamped on both sides of every spread. The shift is half the figure, uniform across a page's elements and capped by the tightest headroom, so a collage moves together rather than distorting. Covers never shift.
nodes.norm_label: d5: one guttermm mirrored by page parity

nodes.label: D6: edit single pages, preview spreads
nodes.rationale: Spreads double the canvas width and complicate per-frame editing; a read-only spread preview is much cheaper than a spread-native editor.
nodes.community_name: Small group: D1: flat page list, not leaves
nodes.norm_label: d6: edit single pages, preview spreads

nodes.label: Collage pages need no schema flag
nodes.rationale: A collage page is an inner-page template with more than one frame; the renderer already composites N frames per surface.
nodes.norm_label: collage pages need no schema flag

nodes.label: Per-frame photo allocation prerequisite
nodes.rationale: One photo per surface would print the same photo in every collage cell; fixed in surface-allocation.ts and must not be reintroduced.

nodes.label: No book_renderer module
nodes.rationale: A book page is just frames, which _composite_canvas already draws; page numbers would be an overlay.

nodes.label: GenerateLayoutView refuses books
nodes.rationale: Books require canvases_meta, which the direct partner sync endpoint does not support.

nodes.label: R1: customer-variable surface count
nodes.rationale: Autosave, restore and the render payload all assumed a fixed surface set; D2 turned this from a risk into a certainty.

nodes.label: R3: gutter parity backwards shows only in print
nodes.norm_label: r3: gutter parity backwards shows only in print

nodes.label: One retention clock (EXPORT_RETENTION_DAYS)
nodes.rationale: expires_at used to promise 30 days while the GC deleted at 14, so a partner fetching on day 20 got a 404. Default 7, production 3.

nodes.label: EXPORT_RETENTION_DAYS_UNDER_PRESSURE defaults to the same value
nodes.rationale: Disk pressure must not silently shorten retention below the expires_at already sent to a partner.
nodes.norm_label: export_retention_days_under_pressure defaults to the same value

nodes.label: expires_at stamped on the row at creation
nodes.rationale: Migration 0012: lowering the env var no longer acts retroactively on files whose expiry was already promised. Deploy the migration before lowering it.
nodes.norm_label: expires_at stamped on the row at creation

nodes.label: API audit trail outlives the data (90 days)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately outlives the data it describes so who touched this order stays answerable.
nodes.norm_label: api audit trail outlives the data (90 days)

nodes.label: DELETE /api/ops/orders/<order_id>/purge
nodes.rationale: Needs all_tenants or api_key because order ids are unique only per key; shared files another surviving order references are kept.

nodes.label: UploadedFile.order_id erasure linkage
nodes.rationale: Autosave once overwrote image_paths with [] every 2 seconds, so the purge deleted rows, reported files_deleted: 0 and left photographs on disk. Recording the order at upload makes erasure provable.

nodes.label: Uploads stored per order
nodes.rationale: An all-tenant purge deletes the directory and so erases what is on disk rather than what the DB can enumerate. A key-scoped purge must leave the folder alone, because it is per order id, not per key.

nodes.label: Purge verification sweep and erasure_complete
nodes.rationale: Re-checks every path after commit and returns residual_files / residual_dirs, so a silently failed deletion cannot report success.

nodes.label: Never delete by blank order_id
nodes.rationale: Blank is the legitimate value for direct partner uploads; such a cleanup would destroy valid current uploads.

nodes.label: PII-free weekly backup tier
nodes.rationale: Customer tables are dumped schema-only and uploads/ is left out, so customer data sits in backups at most 7 days. New customer tables must join PII_TABLES and the test.

nodes.label: Purge ledger (re-erase on restore)
nodes.rationale: Kept outside Postgres so a restore cannot roll it back, with an HMAC and no order id. Entries older than the dump are ignored so an order id reused after erasure survives.

nodes.label: Orphan export sweep (GC_ORPHAN_SWEEP)
nodes.rationale: The one sweep that deletes on the absence of a DB row, which is why it shipped disarmed and needed a deliberate arm; five guards must all hold.

nodes.label: An empty audit table proves nothing
nodes.rationale: APIRequest had no writer until 0014, so a zero count during a leaked-key investigation read as proof a credential was unused when nothing was recorded.
nodes.norm_label: an empty audit table proves nothing

nodes.label: AUDIT_EXEMPT_PREFIXES blind spots
nodes.rationale: render-status alone produced ~1,500 rows an hour in one job; an exemption matching an endpoint that touches customer data would be a silent gap in the erasure trail.
